title: Danbury City Council public-hearing notice — Police Department ordinance amendments (August 17, 2026)
summary: Primary municipal notice scheduling a public hearing on amendments to Police Department Code sections 22-19 through 22-30 and explicitly tying the hearing back to the May 5 agenda item.

evidence.claim: The City of Danbury notice schedules an August 17, 2026 public hearing for amendments to Police Department Code sections 22-19 through 22-30 and states that the original agenda item was on file from May 5, 2026.

caveats: A public-hearing notice proves the hearing was noticed for this ordinance surface; it does not by itself prove the hearing occurred, the ordinance passed, or the final text remained unchanged.

title: Danbury City Council agenda — September 1, 2026
summary: Primary City Council agenda placing the Police Department ordinance amendments and four police appointment communications on the September 1 meeting agenda.

evidence.claim: The September 1 City Council agenda lists the Police Department amendments to sections 22-19 through 22-30 as agenda item 18.
The same agenda lists police-detective appointment communications for Ahlstrin and Perkins and entry-level police-officer appointment communications for Ortega-Gonzalez and Restrepo-Gallo.

caveats: Agenda placement is not proof of adoption or appointment approval; the meeting minutes, vote record, and appointment communications remain necessary for final state and full-identity resolution.

title: Danbury PD late-stage ordinance procedure and appointment deltas
summary: Primary City records extend the issue #2514 chronology from the May proposal to an August public-hearing notice and the September 1 council agenda, while preserving vote, enactment, effective-date, and full officer-identity questions as unresolved.

caveats: The August notice and September agenda establish procedural progression, not final enactment.
Agenda-only surnames are not sufficient to force full legal-name identity matches or assert present employment.
No individual officer citizenship or immigration status is inferred or recorded.

findings: The City noticed an August 17 public hearing specifically for amendments to Police Department Code sections 22-19 through 22-30 and tied that hearing to the May 5 agenda item.
The September 1 City Council agenda carried the same Police Department ordinance amendment surface as item 18, materially extending the primary-source chronology beyond proposal stage.
The September 1 agenda separately carried detective appointment communications for Ahlstrin and Perkins and entry-level officer appointment communications for Ortega-Gonzalez and Restrepo-Gallo.
conclusions: Issue #2514 now has primary municipal evidence for the ordinance's progression from May proposal to August public-hearing notice to September council agenda.

The final enacted text, roll-call vote, effective date, formal ordinance identifier, and appointment outcomes/full identities still require the final minutes, enacted code history, and underlying appointment communications.
counterarguments: An item appearing on a meeting agenda can be amended, tabled, rejected, or otherwise disposed of; agenda placement is not an adoption record.

Surname-only appointment agenda entries can correspond to likely payroll candidates, but cross-source identity matches should remain unresolved until the primary appointment record gives the full identity.
unresolved: September 1, 2026 minutes and roll-call disposition for the Police Department ordinance amendments, including both NO votes reported elsewhere.
Final enacted/codified text, effective date, and formal ordinance or resolution identifier.
Underlying appointment communications and final council disposition for Ahlstrin, Perkins, Ortega-Gonzalez, and Restrepo-Gallo.
Full current sworn-force reconciliation against the 2025 payroll-derived candidate census and all 2026 hires, promotions, retirements, and departures.

title: Research pass: Danbury PD late-stage procedural and appointment records (2026-09-15)
summary: Bounded issue #2514 pass preserving official August public-hearing and September council-agenda records without promoting agenda state to final enactment or inferring officer identity/status beyond the source.

data.research_question: Which primary City of Danbury records extend the police-eligibility ordinance chronology beyond the May proposal and expose additional 2026 sworn-force appointment deltas without overclaiming final enactment or identity?
data.method: Searched the existing Danbury corpus and issue history first, deduped the relevant URLs and canonical IDs, then reviewed the official City Agenda Center public-hearing notice and the official September 1 council agenda. Preserved procedural state and appointment labels exactly as observed and kept final vote, enacted text, and full identity resolution open.
classification_rules: Public-hearing notices and meeting agendas establish procedural state only; they are not promoted to proof of enactment or approval.
Surname-only appointment entries are preserved as source observations and are not force-merged to full person identities without the underlying primary appointment record.
Current employment is not inferred from agenda placement.
Citizenship, immigration status, ethnicity, and national origin are not inferred for any individual officer.

findings.finding: The August 17 public-hearing notice preserves the same sections 22-19 through 22-30 ordinance surface and points back to the May 5 agenda item.

The September 1 agenda carries the ordinance amendments plus four police appointment communications, adding late-stage procedural and personnel-delta evidence while leaving final dispositions unresolved.
